one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban recounts the August 29, 2025 Foundation for Liberty and Prosperity award ceremony at the Manila Polo Club, where First Lady Liza Marcos and Fernando Zobel de Ayala headlined the recognition of 20 law scholars, 5 MBA fellows, and 9 dissertation winners before more than 200 guests, and uses the occasion to launch FLP's next programmatic move: a super-committee on legal ethics chaired by Solicitor General Lelen Berberabe with retired SAJ Telly Bernabe, Bern Siy, Atty. Joel Emerson Gregorio, and Atty. Arvin Paolo Cortez (with former BSP Governor Say Tetangco as adviser), animated by Tessie Sy Coson's dictum that 'it is not enough for lawyers to be talented and patriotic; they must also be ethical and Godly.' He celebrates the FLP Scholars Society -- over 120 alumni in seven years, including bar toppers Sean James Borja (ADMU, 2018) and Kyle Christian Tutor (UP, 2024) and yearly placers -- and previews two flagship projects: the futuristic, AI-powered Museum for Liberty and Prosperity (with architect Jun Palafox's team offering pro bono design and a cornerstone hoped for within CJ Gesmundo's term) and the pro-poor, pro-private Fund for Liberty and Prosperity dedicated to helping MSMEs help themselves. Anchoring the address in the biblical injunction 'to whom much is given, much is required' and a parable of small seeds growing into great trees, he closes with the hope that the next gathering will be at the new museum itself -- a vision he frames as ultimately for God and country.
